text:
anna-support: dropping in an escalation — enterprise customer hit a combo of 401s + duplicate billable requests when bundling our TS SDK with their app. they say it started after upgrading to our @1.9.x runtime. repro + logs below.

sam-eng: thanks anna. can you paste the exact bundler and node version?

anna-support: customer on Node 18.17, webpack 5.88, tsc 5.1. they bundle for both edge and node lambdas.

maria-devex: quick note — we changed default export shape in 1.9.0 (named + default) to help ESM consumers. might be an exports map edgecase.

anna-support: customer sent minimal repro steps: 
1) npm i @redwood/inference@1.9.2
2) import { Redwood } from '@redwood/inference' // or require('@redwood/inference')
3) bundle with webpack 5 -> runtime throws at startup: 

```
Error: Cannot find module 'node:process'
Require stack: .../node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/cjs/index.js
```

and then when they fall back to dynamic import we start seeing intermittent 401s from the hosted API and two identical requests show up in logs ~200ms apart (looks like a retry race). customer got billed twice for the same user request and wants a fix.

eli-ops: 401s + duplicate requests could be from our client retry loop + bundler polyfill changing module identity. if the SDK ends up loaded twice (esm+cjs) each copy might maintain its own token cache leading to parallel auth attempts.

qa-jordan: I captured a snippet of their package.json exports map: 

```
"exports": {
  ".": "./dist/index.js",
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

They don't provide separate import/require entries. bundlers sometimes prefer the top-level and end up resolving CJS into ESM environment.

sam-eng: that exports map is the smoking gun. we recommend dual-entry export map: 

```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
  },
  "./package.json": "./package.json"
}
```

also ensure package.json has "type": "module" in the esm build and the cjs build stays explicit.

maria-devex: for immediate mitigation tell customer to pin @redwood/inference@1.8.5 (last known good) or force a single resolution via webpack alias: 

```
resolve: {
  alias: { '@redwood/inference': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.js') }
}
```

anna-support: customer tried pinning to 1.8.5 and 401s stopped, but they still hit double-request billing on serverless cold starts (we think retries + lambda warmup).

eli-ops: can we confirm our client retry semantics? are we deduping in-flight auth token refreshes?

sam-eng: we have a token refresh promise cached on SDK instance level. if there are two independent SDK instances (different module copies), they won't share that promise. hence parallel refresh and duplicate outbound calls. code-wise the fix: make public entry expose a singleton token manager on globalThis for Node/browser where appropriate, guarded like: 

```
if (!globalThis.__REDWOOD_TOKEN_MANAGER) {
  globalThis.__REDWOOD_TOKEN_MANAGER = new TokenManager();
}
module.exports.tokenManager = globalThis.__REDWOOD_TOKEN_MANAGER;
```

maria-devex: also add a check in our bundler CI matrix for webpack/rollup/next to catch single-export maps. add tests that install and bundle a tiny app and assert only one copy of the SDK exists at runtime.

qa-jordan: filed a quick unit + integration test PR to cover global singleton + dual exports map detection.

anna-support: customer also observed TypeScript types missing when they import directly from deep path `@redwood/inference/dist/esm/index.js`. they complained editor saw no types.

sam-eng: ensure we publish type declarations next to both esm and cjs builds and update package.json: 

```
"types": "dist/types/index.d.ts",
"exports": {
  ".": { "import": "./dist/esm/index.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js", "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts" }
}
```

(note: npm ignores non-root types exports entries, so we still ship a top-level "types" key).

eli-ops: ops ask — did customer show exact billing entries? I want request ids to correlate.

anna-support: provided two request ids: req_01FXAAA, req_01FXAAB  (200ms apart). both show identical payload and same user id.

sam-eng: I can trace those in logs. looks like auth-refresh started at t0, two outbound calls to /v1/auth/refresh with same client id. server accepted both -> each resulted in token issue logged and then both original requests retried by the client. that's why double billing happened.

maria-devex: proposed action items: 
- patch release 1.9.3: add dual-entry exports, publish types, add global singleton guard, and a small runtime check that logs a warning if multiple instances detected.
- release note + migration guide for bundlers.
- add CI bundler smoke tests.

anna-support: customer would like ETA. can we do hotfix?

sam-eng: I can cut 1.9.3 today with the singleton guard + exports map adjustments. QA to validate on webpack/next.

qa-jordan: will smoke test against their provided repro and confirm dedupe; estimating 4 hours.

eli-ops: recommend we offer a credit for the duplicate billing while we patch. finance ok with a small one-off credit for clearly duplicate requests.

anna-support: I'll coordinate with customer and send workaround steps (pin to 1.8.5 or alias) and offer credit.

dev-bot: deploy pipeline started for tag v1.9.3-hotfix by sam-eng. CI build 2026-03-17T09:12:00Z.

sam-eng: pinging @maria-devex for docs blurb, @eli-ops for billing flow. Will post release PR link when ready.

maria-devex: got it, I'll draft a short "Bundling, ESM/CJS and duplicate auth" guide and add to devdocs.

anna-support: thanks team — I'll update the customer thread and escalate if they need a patch earlier. :heart:
